sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Build and publish the website
sections.what: Builds the site and publishes it to the GitHub Pages address. It runs on each push to main, when started by hand, and when the snapshot job finishes. The build stage prepares the files and the deploy stage publishes them.
sections.why: Likely reason: publishing on each change keeps the live site current, and waiting for the snapshot job lets new images go out with the site.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here checks whether the snapshot job succeeded, so the site still publishes after a failed capture.

summary: Builds the website and publishes it to GitHub Pages on each push to main, on a manual start, and after the snapshot job finishes.
purpose: Put the current version of the site online without manual steps.
why: Likely reason: publishing on each change keeps the live site current, and waiting for the snapshot job lets new images go out with the site. Not stated in the code.
how: Two stages run in order. The build stage checks out the code, sets up Node.js 20 with its package cache, runs npm ci to install exact dependency versions, runs npm run build, and uploads the output folder ./out as a Pages artifact. The deploy stage then publishes that artifact to GitHub Pages. A concurrency group named pages makes runs queue rather than overlap.
inputs: A push to main, a manual start, or the finish of the snapshot workflow. The package and lock files and the site source, none of which are in the packet.
outputs: A built site in ./out, published to GitHub Pages, with the page address shown on the deployment record.
risks: The trigger from the snapshot workflow does not check whether that workflow succeeded, so a failed capture still leads to a publish. The build depends on files not in the packet, such as the lock file.
debug: Open the run in the Actions tab. A failed build stage points to npm ci or npm run build, so read those logs first. A failed deploy stage often means GitHub Pages is not enabled for the repository or permissions are missing. If the live site looks old, check which run deployed last.
